candidates.comment: Thanks for the report. The same persistent Keep failure and “changes were updated after they were shown” error are tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/345263. This report also adds Copilot Fusion in agent mode and comparison tabs that keep loading even after reopening comparisons, reloading the window, and restarting VS Code; those details belong with that investigation.

Thanks for the detailed logs and stable-release confirmation. This is the workspace-change session-deletion problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/343406. This report adds an important reproduction: editing an existing saved .code-workspace on macOS arm64 in 1.145.2 destroys loaded sessions, while later routine shutdowns preserve their histories. Those details should remain part of the investigation there.

Thanks for the detailed report. This matches the enterprise SDK authentication failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338596, where Copilot mode fails with the same 401 while Local chat works. Your additional details—GHEC EU data residency, Windows 11, bundled SDK 1.0.73, and a successful standalone CLI 1.0.89 request—are useful diagnostic evidence for that investigation.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is the same mode-picker failure tracked by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/316908: changing modes erases an unsent draft and submits `Start implementation` without user intent. Your Agent-to-Ask/Plan reproduction and the resulting unintended workspace changes add useful coverage to that investigation.

Thanks for the feedback. The request to preserve a Classic UI option, including the concern about extra whitespace, is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326146. This report adds Windows 1.133.0 and smaller-screen context to that request.

For now, `"workbench.experimental.modernUI": false` restores Classic UI, while `"window.density.layout": "compact"` reduces spacing within the modern UI. Compact Mode is not a promise to retain Classic UI permanently.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/327167 tracks the same problem: same-named MCP servers from multiple plugins appear without enough source information. This report adds the Slack example and the misleading Workspace grouping, where opening a server's location reveals a plugin instead; those details belong with that work.

Thanks for the report. The apparent stall after clicking Commit without a message, and the need to explain that the message should be completed in the editor, are already discussed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/193935. This report adds an affected Windows 11 setup on VS Code 1.129.0 and a specific request for an explanatory prompt.

Thanks for the report. The same administrator-launch failure with code 18 is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/249527. This report adds an occurrence on VS Code 1.128.0 and Windows 10 build 19045 to that investigation.

Thanks for the request. Support for working with the whole configured workspace in the Agents App is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/311148, including opening multi-root workspace files and working across their folders.

Thanks for the request. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/8ec672b4c998523e921aefe7f3bc831e0bb77a82 added `sessions.useWorktree`: set it to `false` to default new workspaces to working directly in the existing checkout. For a workspace with a saved choice, clear **New Worktree** before starting the session; that choice is remembered per workspace. Edits then reach the checkout your development server watches without merging an agent branch. The fix shipped in 1.138.0.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/315699 tracks the same gap: selecting a worktree in Source Control does not switch the files and the rest of the working context. Let's consolidate there, retaining your specific example that the branch indicator changes while the editor still shows files from the previous worktree—consistent checkout identity should be part of that experience.

Thanks for the detailed logs and follow-up. This matches the authenticated-but-unusable Chat failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/307335, including returning to Sign In after sending a message. Consolidating there should retain this report's Fedora reproduction, Windows confirmation, and successful CLion comparison using the same account; the permissions-setting workaround reported there has not been confirmed for your setup.

Thanks for the report. The signed-out model picker and its missing sign-in or upgrade entry point are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/297149. This report adds `code-insiders --transient` as a concrete reproduction of the Auto-only dropdown; that case should be covered by the same work.

Thanks for the report. This is the same light-theme breadcrumb border tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/301248. Your diagnosis adds an important detail: it uses editorWidget.border, so editorGroupHeader.border no longer hides it, while changing the widget border also affects unrelated surfaces. Consolidating under the older report; the maintainer's direction in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321248#issuecomment-4744329965 is to remove this separator.

Thanks for the detailed report and the profile. This turns out not to be a Fedora/D-Bus-specific issue — the `--prof-startup` CLI code was passing a malformed `host:port` value to the renderer/extension-host debug-port flags, which broke the inspector connection and caused the 'FAILED to start profiling' errors and the 15s timeout you saw. That was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/72cfebb6ffada6ae87d98440dddeed88b9968cd8 (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/307849) and shipped in VS Code 1.116.0. Please try `--prof-startup` again on the latest build and reopen if it still fails.

Thanks for the report. The disabled-looking Update button is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/293036. This report adds the Light+ (Default Light+) case on Windows with VS Code 1.109.3, affects both enabled and disabled extensions, and highlights installation-status visibility; those details should remain part of the same review.

Thanks for the report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/182401098564c84f2ff76906bce37c73e6f17d82 added a check after cloud-session loading so concurrent opens reuse the existing chat model instead of appending its messages again. That check remains on current main, so this can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.110.1.

Thanks for the report. This is the same chat model-resolution failure tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/287262. This occurrence adds that GPT-5.1 Codex Max was selected on macOS arm64 when the resolver unexpectedly requested the `gpt-4.1` family.

Thanks for the report. This matches https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/287263: GPT-4.1 family resolution fails even though a Claude model is selected. Linking this report preserves the additional Claude Opus 4.5 Agent-mode context and the terminal sequence preceding the error.

Thanks for the report. Auto could pair a session token with a different model when its selected model was missing from the local endpoint cache. This was fixed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/83915df69898ab35baf343adea9b40772d0e5e94: Auto now resolves against the complete model list and no longer substitutes an unrelated model for that session. Closing as fixed. The fix shipped in 1.116.0.

Thanks for the detailed examples. The same non-English plain-text-to-INI misdetection is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/131450, including a maintainer-confirmed Cyrillic example. Your paired 20/21-character cases across several scripts and punctuation provide useful additional evidence for that issue.

Thanks for the report and the follow-up reproduction details. The stale selection and one-match results are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/237774. This report adds a useful case: retained find/replace strings can narrow the selection, and refocusing the find input still uses the old scope; clearing the inputs before reopening is a workaround. Those cases should also be checked when reviewing https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331038.

Thanks for the report and request IDs. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/253136, which tracks the same Copilot request-failure outcome, including service-side disruptions; the long-running GPT-5.1 Codex Mini refactoring context remains useful evidence there.

Thanks for the detailed report. https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/154913 already tracks notebook searches starting at the top and losing position after individual replacements. This report adds clear Ctrl+H and repeated Replace steps on Windows 11 24H2 with VS Code 1.105.1 and 1.106.0-insider, including confirmation with extensions disabled.

Thanks for the report. The recurring disappearance of VS Code around Windows updates, requiring reinstallation, is already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/52855. This report adds Code 1.104.1 on Windows build 26100, recurrence across four or five updates, and confirmation that settings remain intact.

Thanks for the detailed follow-up. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/253136, whose discussion includes the same Copilot Chat 413 failure; carrying over the useful details here that it occurred with trivial prompts and no context on Windows after launching from Anaconda Prompt, together with the shutdown hang.

Thanks for the report. This matches the Explorer jump when returning from another window tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/245392. This report also captures macOS 1.103.2, dragging the wrong file, and the distinction when the second window's file is already open in the first window; those details should remain part of the investigation.

Thanks for the context. The requested environment setup landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/aead51d8a2ae0d7ba66375249bc7cafdbc861714: coding-agent setup now prepares dependencies, native build prerequisites, and Electron/Playwright before the session starts. The repository instructions also cover scoped compilation and unit tests, with further validation-cost improvements in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/573eff8eb4f79194d31977e4c4d8c9dd6ec1e852, so this request can be closed as completed. The fix shipped in 1.105.0.

Thanks for the report and confirmation. The missing entry in Windows Default apps is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/191782, with registration changes proposed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/293033. This report adds confirmation for VS Code 1.101.1 user setup on Windows 11 24H2, plus the missing persistent association choices for .ipynb and .txt; those details should remain part of the investigation.

Thanks for the detailed sample. We're tracking language-detection failures in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/131450, which also reports JavaScript pasted into an untitled document being detected as Dart. This report adds a reproducible HTML/JavaScript sample on Windows 11 without Dart extensions, a JSON confirmation, and suggestions for language exclusions or a plain-text fallback; those details remain useful for that investigation.

Thanks for the report. The same Quick Open failure with folder-prefixed paths is tracked in the older open issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/208840. This report adds the useful renamed-folder case (`name: "Source"`, `path: "code"`, searching for `code/main.py`); the open candidate https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/318517 explicitly covers that case, but has not merged.

Thanks for the report. The same context-menu focus transfer is tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/212679. This report adds a Windows 11 reproduction with the webview moved below the editor using workbench.action.moveEditorToBelowGroup, and the observation that moving it to the right avoids the issue; those details should remain part of the investigation.

Thanks for the report. Named capture references being inserted literally in editor replacements are already tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/195724. The JavaScript replacement syntax is `$<g>` rather than `${g}`, but that support remains missing. Your Windows 1.86.2 example and observation that `${g}` previously worked are linked in that discussion; no regression range has been established.

Thanks for the detailed report. This is covered by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/147218, which includes deletion commands targeting the background editor instead of the Command Palette input and explicitly includes `deleteWordLeft`. Your macOS `Ctrl+W` example, the ineffective `textInputFocus` binding, and the working native `Alt+Backspace` behavior provide additional reproduction details for that request.

Thanks for the report and keyboard logs. This matches the AltGr cursor-left problem tracked in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/24783. Your log shows `key: AltGraph` arriving with `code: ArrowLeft` and invoking `cursorLeft` before `[` is inserted; it also records that `"keyboard.dispatch": "keyCode"` avoids the problem while default dispatch still failed in 1.89.0. Consolidating there preserves these diagnostic details alongside the existing reports.

Thanks for the request. Windows 11 primary context-menu integration was enabled for stable builds in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/3e56b3a2a4002a63b82bdcfdb7ea5873dbc6957e, so “Open with Code” can appear directly on folders without Shift+right-click. This completes the requested capability; installation cases where the entry still does not appear are tracked separately, including https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/304214. The fix shipped in 1.109.0.

Thanks for filing this. Current `main` already does exactly what's described: `resolveNLSConfiguration` in src/vs/base/node/nls.ts takes the fast default-locale path whenever `userLocale.startsWith('en')`, so `en-GB` and any other `en-*` dialect skip the on-disk language-pack lookup just like plain `en`. That change landed in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/d65fd5ba2e7202cac14316c2935680222e1af9cb. Closing as completed — please reopen if you still see the waterfall for an `en-*` locale on current builds. The fix shipped in 1.92.0.
